channel.description: Latest articles from Monterey County Herald (montereyherald.com)

item.title: Pesticide regulators sued for “confusing, contradictory rules”
item.description: It's the fourth time since 2017 that advocates and DPR have gone to court over 1,3-D, a fumigant widely used to kill pests on Monterey County crops, like strawberries. 1,3-D has been linked to increased cancer risk, especially for those living and working near application zones.

item.title: Two rain storms landing in Monterey County
item.description: A wind advisory remains in effect until 4 a.m. Wednesday. The National Weather Service is reporting south winds of 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 50 mph expected. The affected areas include the Interior Central Coast, South Monterey Bay and the Big Sur Coast.

item.title: Privacy activists call on California to remove covert license plate readers
item.description: Critics argue this surveillance may violate the Fourth Amendment.

item.title: Detroit Tigers bring back former ace Justin Verlander, 2025 SF Giants starter
item.description: Verlander bounced back from an injury-plagued season in 2024 and a slow start last season to post a 3.83 ERA in 29 starts with the Giants.

item.title: Moderna says FDA refuses its application for new mRNA flu vaccine
item.description: Moderna received a “refusal-to-file” letter, objecting to its clinical trial methods.

item.title: SF Giants’ new manager Vitello officially begins first MLB spring training
item.description: The Giants began spring training on Tuesday in Scottsdale with pitchers and catchers reporting

item.title: Close Maduro ally pardoned by Biden once again a target of US criminal investigation
item.description: Alex Saab is under scrutiny again for his involvement in Venezuela's CLAP program.

item.title: Federal judge dismisses attempt to obtain Michigan voter data in latest rejection of DOJ
item.description: The DOJ sued at least 23 states and the District of Columbia for voter data.

item.title: Why SF Giants believe in Arráez’s defense at second base despite shaky metrics
item.description: Arráez's one-year, $12 million deal became official on Tuesday afternoon

item.title: Former federal prosecutor who quit amid Trump administration dispute now representing Don Lemon
